fresh_checks: C11 contact points: a Lipschitz gradient maps a null set to a null set; the slope ball gives second-order Taylor contact in any specified neighborhood, with error 2 delta I.

Measurable strong maximum principle: strict weak comparison uses good Taylor points and a local coefficient upper bound; annular exponential barrier has positive image and contradicts vanishing gradient at an extremum, without differentiating coefficients.

Cofactor comparison 2^(-(n-1)) H^(n-1)<=T<=H^(n-1) and eigenproducts; bounded coefficients make its real symbol uniformly elliptic exactly on the essential-positive H locus for n>=2, with the curve case elliptic everywhere.

Extremum anchors: perturbed Hessian contact (1+s)B>=A+sC first makes B and then A positive. Trace and determinant of the normalized matrices give B^n>=C^n. Taylor approximations pass this inequality using density continuity, not Hessian continuity.

Positive density plus bounded Hessians gives a local eigenvalue lower bound. Strong maximum principle gives constants on extremal components and their closures; the connected, dense two-component and meeting-closure criteria follow. A connected embedded hypersurface has at most two complement components without a chosen global side.

Square-root threshold: nonnegative C11 density has zero gradient on its zero set and a quadratic upper bound. Transverse segments through a separating zero set give volume >=c sqrt(t); overlapping coordinate-ball labels then prove global connectedness. Dominated convergence handles f^(-1/2).

Weighted energy: dd c(w^2)=2w dd c w+(i/pi) partial w wedge bar partial w; C2 approximation against a continuous positive weighted cofactor gives zero positive gradient integral. Polarization annihilates the range and constancy propagates along absolutely continuous reachable curves.

Real cofactor symbol: the x,y block matrix [P,Q;-Q,P]/(8 pi) and the complex Hessian conversion have correct signs and factor. Positivity, absence of first order terms and its range identification are checked.

Exterior tangent-ball propagation: shrink the nearest-point ball, use the negative-image exponential barrier on a lens, then extend its upper contact outside the ball. A non-kernel exterior normal gives a contradiction. Squared-distance upper derivative and Lipschitz range fields give flow invariance by Gronwall.

Bracket generation: pushed-forward range fields span an invariant distribution containing all iterated brackets. Independent pushed-forward fields and the inverse function theorem make every orbit open; connectedness yields one orbit. No constant rank or smooth square root is assumed.

Unweighted energy defect and dimensions: its sign is one half the w^2 pairing with dd c T. A surface has dd c T=2 dd c omega; in dimension three the expansion has both 3 dd c(omega^2) and 3 dd c omega wedge dd c(u+v), so Gauduchon alone does not remove the second term.

Low-dimensional determinant algebra: equality of positive determinants gives D^2<=0 in dimension two and 2C D^2<=0 in dimension three, with equality only at A=B. Strong W2,n approximation passes all products, including the signed torsion identity and L3/2 gradient-square limit; the sign assumption gives the opposite integral sign.

Sobolev rigidity: distributional dd c w=0 has a global psh representative, hence compact connected maximum-principle rigidity. Canonical qpsh representatives upgrade almost-everywhere equality. For C2 dense positivity, semipositive zero-determinant algebra keeps the integral sign and continuity finishes the argument.

Weak extremum localization: Minkowski and strict positivity reserve control both parts of a thin sublevel. The coefficient gives B>=(1-kappa^(1/n))/2 times its equation mass; retained smooth positive volume makes that mass nonzero. Infimum perturbation bounds locate a near-extreme set.

Weak level energy: local radial convolution, closed-product integration identities and uniform weights define an intrinsic finite positive energy measure and the chain rule. Its level pushforward has second derivative sigma; zero total and first moments identify the compactly supported Lipschitz density k(t), so no level has energy mass.

Weak coercivity: interior convolution gives a lower determinant bound for the absolutely continuous Hessian. Strong local W1,2 convergence and Fatou give the energy lower measure. The cofactor eigenvalue is at least det/trace; finite trace mass and Cauchy--Schwarz control the L1 Sobolev derivative.

Null extreme levels: reciprocal k+delta transition profiles have energy at most 1/J. Local coercivity makes their indicator limit have zero distributional gradient on connected U; density of U supplies a nonempty positive side, hence the extreme set has zero equation mass.

Concentrating smooth tests: classical smooth ball Dirichlet solvability is retained as an input. Gradient area formula and det_R S<=4^n det_C(Hess)^2 give a uniform sup bound from the L2 density norm. Smooth convex cutoff and finite averaging preserve a strict background reserve and determinant >=epsilon g independent of density derivatives and height.

Bounded connected uniqueness: concentrate the test on the compact null extreme set at F>=epsilon/2 while dominating the complementary part by epsilon. A uniform kappa and a thin near-minimum set contradict weak extremum localization. Globally bounded measurable positive densities use coercivity on all X and essential upper bounds.

Invariant mass comparison and uniqueness: max locality plus ordered contact give ordinary comparison by subtracting finite common mass. The converse follows by constant shifts. Auxiliary indicator density 2F 1_S+b0 has exactly mass V; Minkowski gives a factor >1, comparison gives zero mass and domination contradicts separated extrema.

Projective rank directions: local homogeneous-lift independence, the nonzero radial tau component, three independent rank-one forms, cube factor 6, chain rule and logistic Fubini--Study coefficients all agree.

Open zero-band construction: the flat bump and reflected cutoffs give both scalar cancellations; endpoint gluing is smooth. Exact correction restores horizontal positivity at the two rank-one levels while preserving positive transition regions. The differential dr wedge((x-prime-z)P+(y-prime+z)Q) proves nonclosedness.

Radial continuum: the transition balance has an intervals worth of unique positive J choices. Piecewise slope stays between -p and p, is Lipschitz and continuous at the switches, so no hypersurface Hessian term appears. C11 products give the desired cube, distinct slopes remain distinct after normalization, and the symmetric pair gives an invariant solution.

Thin-zero smooth family: scalar ODE uniqueness and strict lower barriers backwards/forwards trap h/p in a compact subset of (-1,1). Interior continuation gives the whole band. The scaled rational ODE gives polynomial growth of all quotient derivatives; exponential flatness then gives smooth zero extensions.

Quadratic-zero family: finite-order coefficient zeros give the stated density. ODE lower barriers and h<0 yield h-prime=h L with L>=C/p on the left and <=-C/p on the right. Since p is comparable to distance squared, slopes and every derivative decay as exp(-A/d) times a polynomial, hence extend flatly.

Real analytic example: positive divided differences define H without singular endpoint division. Both radicands stay positive; q D=z E gives determinant cancellation and the prescribed product d. Positive-coefficient patching fixes the radial coefficient by d/(xy), and the exact correction makes a nonclosed Hermitian background.

Analytic zero geometry and higher dimensions: t is a global real analytic ratio; its two connected regular levels are quadratic zeros. Product expansion has exactly binomial(n,3), preserves density relative to Omega_n^n and rank n-1. Tubular coordinates give sqrt(s) sublevel volume and inverse-power integrability iff alpha<1/2.

Cross-criterion consistency: analytic examples have three positive-density components and the same missing cofactor direction at the zero levels. Extremal outer closures are disjoint; adjacency through the middle component does not imply propagation. No open question closure or new external proof certification is claimed.
